NewAgent.title: New AI Assistant
NewAgent.description: Answer the questions: the more detailed you are, the better the agent will perform in real conversations.

AgentWizard.reviewIntro: Done! Review the summary below and save to create the agent.

name.question: What do you want to call this agent? It's the name you'll recognize it by among your assistants (e.g. "Outreach for marketing agencies").

companyName.question: What's the name of your company or the product this agent represents?

valueProp.question: What do you do, in one sentence? (your value proposition)

differentiation.question: Why should a prospect choose you over the competition?

icp.question: Who is your ideal customer? (role, industry, company size)
icp.placeholder: E.g. founder or head of growth at B2B agencies with 5-50 people

tone.question: What tone should the assistant use?
tone.placeholder: Type a custom tone or pick one below

goal.question: What's the end goal of the conversation?
goal.placeholder: Type a custom goal or pick one below

language.question: What language should the assistant write in?
language.placeholder: Type a custom language or pick one below

objective.question: What's this agent's main objective?
objective.placeholder: Type a custom objective or pick one below

products.question: What products or services do you offer?
products.placeholder: E.g. a monthly SEO retainer and one-off website audits...

calendarLink.question: Booking link (Calendly, HubSpot, Cal.com...) to send when the prospect is ready to schedule a call.

objections.question: Are there common objections the agent should handle? The more detail you give, the better it will respond.
objections.placeholder: E.g. "Too expensive" → respond by explaining the average customer ROI...

guardrails.question: Is there anything the agent should never say or do?
guardrails.placeholder: E.g. never discuss pricing, never promise discounts...

Connections.title: Connections
Connections.description: Connect a LinkedIn profile via the cloud runner (in runner/): a LinkedIn session cookie authenticates a headless browser as if you were logging in from another device — no need to keep Chrome open.
Connections.warning: The runner performs real actions on your LinkedIn account (connection requests, messages). LinkedIn may flag the login as a "new device" and ask for verification the first time. Test it on a secondary account first, with low limits — see runner/README.md in the repo. (The Chrome extension in extension/ is still available as an alternative.)

ConnectionsClient.deleteConfirm: Delete this connection? Linked campaigns will stay active but without an executor.
ConnectionsClient.cookiePlaceholder: Paste the li_at cookie value here
ConnectionsClient.setupTitle: Connection "{label}" created — set up the runner
ConnectionsClient.setupStep2: 2. LinkedIn session cookie (li_at) — it's like a password: whoever has it can act as you on LinkedIn. To find it: go to linkedin.com already logged in → open DevTools (F12) → Application (or Storage) → Cookies → linkedin.com → copy the value of the li_at cookie.
ConnectionsClient.skipHint: You can also skip this step now and add it later from the connections list below.
ConnectionsClient.setupCliStep2: Copy runner/.env.example to runner/.env and set the site URL + token.
ConnectionsClient.setupCliStep3: npm start — see runner/README.md for details and risk warnings.
